case.pattern_description: Online purchase 3523199 used a device not seen on this card, shortly after in-person activity. That mixed-channel shift is treated as stolen credentials rather than a stolen card number alone.

evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3523199 is a 100.07 USD online product-R purchase in billing region 330.0 on 2016-12-07 21:38:37. Card C02923-K1 is a visa credit owned by C02923.
Region 330.0 has 85 prior purchases on this card before the alert.
Closed cases on this card: CC-2400 (confirmed_fraud, account_takeover); CC-2717 (confirmed_fraud, account_takeover); CC-2857 (confirmed_fraud, account_takeover).
Device iOS Device | iOS 9.3.5 | mobile safari 9.0 | 1024x768 is also linked to 3 other card(s): C02354-K2, C07987-K2, C08299-K1.
Email domain gmail.com is present on the flagged purchase; email_fanout found 26 other cards, treated as too common for R6.
Billing region 330.0 appears on 11 other cards in the local 1-hop fan-out. Region sharing is recorded, not treated as proof of a shared origin.
Supports legitimate: flagged amount and channel match established spend on card C02923-K1.
Supports fraud: new device, mixed-channel takeover, or a tight shared-origin cluster is present on the neighborhood.
Episode reconstruction grouped 3 transactions around 3523199 using history, device, amount outliers, and NEXT edges 3509459, 3532043.
Customer denied the purchase and still has the card.
R6 Shared origin: Several cards with fraud associated with the same device profile, billing region, or recipient email: CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT, and MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS for every affected card.
Account takeover: Mixed-channel behavior inconsistent with the cardholder, often with device and match-flag anomalies. Stolen credentials, not only a stolen card number.

Closed case CC-0255: Case CC-0255: cardholder C02354 reported unrecognized activity on card C02354-K2. 7 transaction(s) between 2016-07-06 and 2016-07-08 totaling $1,167.08 were confirmed fraudulent. Mixed-channel activity inconsistent with the cardholder; credentials and card data both used. Online transactions came from a iOS Device on mobile safari 10.0. Card blocked and reissued. Customer reimbursed.

FFIEC authentication guidance: FFIEC guidance expects layered authentication. A new device or credential change on an online purchase is a reason to step up authentication, not automatic proof of fraud.

case.summary: HHG-005 is a risk_score alert on a 100.07 USD online purchase in billing region 330.0. Graph history shows 85 prior purchases in that region. Pattern is account_takeover; fraud probability 0.81. Episode size 3; exposure 334.10 USD. Verdict is fraud.

evidence_requests.assumed_response: Step-up authentication failed. Customer still has the card.
